{{Current events|year=2021|month=03|day=23|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**A bombing in [[Chaman]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]], near to [[Afghanistan-Pakistan border|the border]] with [[Afghanistan]], kills three people and wounds 13 others. The [[Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-blast/three-killed-13-injured-in-blast-at-pakistani-afghan-border-idUSKBN2BF2HO (Reuters)]
*[[Naxalite insurgency]]
**At least five security personnel and a driver are killed when [[Naxalite]]s attack their in bus with an [[Improvised explosive device|IED]] as it cross a bridge over a culvert in [[Chhattisgarh]], [[India]]. This is the biggest Naxalite attack of the year so far in the region. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/raipur/chhattisgarh-5-jawans-killed-as-maoists-target-bus-carrying-security-forces-in-bastar/articleshow/81652848.cms (Times of India)].

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2020 California wildfires]]
**[[Zogg Fire]]
***Investigations into the 2020 fire that destroyed 56,338 acres in northern [[California]] conclude the fire began when a [[Pinus sabiniana|grey pine]] tree fell on power lines belonging to the [[Pacific Gas and Electric Company]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/deadly-blaze-caused-by-pg-26e-power-lines-contacting-pine-tree/ar-BB1eRgzf?ocid=uxbndlbing (Bloomberg via MSN)] [https://www.sfchronicle.com/california-wildfires/article/Deadly-Zogg-Fire-started-when-tree-fell-on-PG-E-16045411.php (San Francisco Chronicle)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[President of South Korea|President]] [[Moon Jae-in]] receives a dose of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] in preparation for visiting the [[United Kingdom]] for the [[G7]] summit in June. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/asia-pacific/544436-south-koreas-moon-gets-astrazeneca-vaccine (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tajikistan]]
****[[Tajikistan]] begins their [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccination]] drive against [[COVID-19]] on the orders of [[President of Tajikistan|President]] [[Emomali Rahmon]]. [https://akipress.com/news:655902:Tajikistan_starts_vaccination_against_Covid-19/ (AKIPress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 333 new fatalities from COVID-19 in the last 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 30,431. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/covid-19-in-ukraine-11476-new-cases-333-new-deaths-121928-total-vaccinations.html (''Kyiv Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] receives a dose of a domestically-produced COVID-19 [[vaccine]]; it is unknown which of Russia's current three vaccine candidates were administered. Earlier in the day, the [[Government of Russia|government]] had announced this ambiguity was deliberate, before noting that "all three Russian-made vaccines are absolutely reliable and effective." [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/name-of-vaccine-russias-vladimir-putin-to-take-will-be-a-secret-says-kremlin/ar-BB1eRQzR?ocid=uxbndlbing (Reuters via MSN)]
**[[Pfizer]] says that they plan to develop new vaccines for other viruses following the success of their [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccine]] candidate. [https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2021/03/23/pfizer-to-reportedly-develop-new-vaccines-on-its-own-using-mrna-technology.html (CNBC)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Boulder shooting]]
**The suspect in yesterday's [[mass shooting]] in [[Boulder, Colorado]], which resulted in the killing of ten people, is [[criminal charge|charged]] with ten counts of [[murder (United States law)|murder]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/03/23/us/boulder-colorado-shooting-tuesday/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Israeli legislative election]] 
**[[Israelis]] go to the polls for the fourth time in less than two years. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-56483277 (BBC)]
*[[Killing of Jamal Khashoggi]]
**[[Agnès Callamard]], [[United Nations special rapporteur|Special Rapporteur]] appointed by the [[United Nations Human Rights Council]], reveals a senior [[Saudi Arabia]]n official twice threatened to have her "taken care of" if the UN did not obstruct her investigation of the assassination of [[Jamal Khashoggi]]. Khashoggi, who had been critical of the al-Saud dynasty, was murdered and dismembered by Saudi agents in the [[Saudi Arabia–Turkey relations|Saudi Arabian consulate in Istanbul]] in 2018 under what is believed to be the direct orders of Saudi [[Mohammed_bin_Salman|Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/mar/23/top-saudi-official-issued-death-threat-against-uns-khashoggi-investigator (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**During a news conference in [[Naypyitaw]], the [[Tatmadaw]] defend the reimposition of the [[Military junta|junta]] and claim that ousted [[State Counsellor of Myanmar|national leader]] [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] was corrupt, tantamount to [[Graft (politics)|graft]]. No supporting evidence for these allegations was offered outside of the taped testimony of a former colleague of Aung San Suu Kyi, [[Phyo Min Thein]], who has been detained by the military since the coup began. [https://apnews.com/article/aung-san-suu-kyi-myanmar-yangon-f2f63948a58ab67781e1763e1b070c61 (AP)]
